title: SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot: structured document generation with Forms
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap, Microsoft's notice and Learn support its availability, licensing, permissions and documented limitations. Minor corrections are needed to the action rating, the licence-assignment checklist item and the wording about published forms being read-only.

claims.claim: Submitting a form generates a new document with submitted values merged into the template fields.

claims.claim: Power Automate does not apply conditional field visibility, so a field hidden in the form can be visible in the generated document.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Limits
claims.claim: Word for the web does not re-evaluate conditional sections when field values change after generation.
claims.quote: In a generated document opened in Word for the web, conditional sections don't update when you change a field value after generation—the hidden and shown sections stay as they were at generation time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Limits
claims.claim: Published forms are read-only in SharePoint.
claims.quote: Forms are read-only once published. To make structural field changes, edit the template in Word and republish. ... Make non-structural changes such as showing or hiding fields, changing themes, and updating settings directly in the SharePoint form view.
claims.fix: Replace 'Published forms are read-only in SharePoint' and 'forms are read-only once published' with 'Published form fields require Word for structural changes; visibility, themes and settings remain editable in SharePoint', as qualified at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/copilot-in-sharepoint-structured-document-generation.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature page states no licence requirement or extra charge for form submitters.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation Copilot Credits licensing submitters. Read feature prerequisites and requirements in full: licence assigned to creators; submitters need only the form link. No submitter licence or extra charge is stated.

claims.claim: Advanced work in Copilot in SharePoint uses Copilot Credits through usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Advanced work requires usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The Copilot in SharePoint page does not state whether structured document generation counts as advanced work.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation Copilot Credits licensing submitters. Read Get started with Copilot in SharePoint in full, including its licensing capabilities table; structured document generation is not named or assigned to the advanced-work category.

claims.claim: The feature page publishes no price for template-design time or library storage.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation Copilot Credits licensing submitters. Read Generate structured documents in a SharePoint document library in full; it describes templates and library storage but gives no price for either.

claims.claim: Beyond Copilot's analysis of template content to suggest fields, Learn does not describe other Copilot processing for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation processing autonomous guests. Read the full feature page, including Detect potential fields, document generation and metadata capture; no additional Copilot processing mechanism is described beyond template field detection.

claims.claim: The feature page describes no autonomous generation, while separately documenting Power Automate generation.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation processing autonomous guests. Read the full feature page: form submission and configured Power Automate workflows are described, but no autonomous agent deciding to generate documents is documented.

claims.claim: Copilot in SharePoint has a Site AI panel for site-level availability options.
claims.quote: The Site AI settings panel lets site owners manage how users interact with AI on their site, including Copilot in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an availability control respected by Copilot in SharePoint.
claims.quote: If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that Site AI options govern structured document generation.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation Restricted Content Discovery Site AI. Read feature and Copilot in SharePoint get-started pages. Site AI options concern the header agent, Copilot button for page visitors and advanced document processing, not document generation forms.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether Restricted Content Discovery governs structured document generation forms.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation Restricted Content Discovery Site AI. Read feature and get-started pages and restricted-content-discovery excerpts. Restrictions cover Copilot and AI entry points, not expressly Forms > Document generation form or submissions through existing links.

claims.claim: Microsoft Forms has its own on/off setting.
claims.quote: If you're an admin, you can set up Microsoft Forms, then turn it off or turn it on again for your entire organization or just specific people.

claims.claim: Whether the Microsoft Forms on/off setting governs forms created in SharePoint libraries is not confirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation Forms tenant admin disable switch PowerShell Microsoft Graph; structured document generation PowerShell Graph disable processing Microsoft Forms. Read Forms on/off and feature pages; neither connects the Forms service setting to SharePoint document generation.

claims.claim: The feature page refers to users in the organisation but does not settle whether guests can submit forms.
claims.quote: Searched: structured document generation processing autonomous guests. Read the full feature page: 'share the form link so users in your organization can submit forms' and 'Form submitters need only the form link'; guest or external-user eligibility is not stated.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits the standard for this launched, on-by-default feature with medium risk and cost and a decision to take.
claims.quote: Fields: status 'launched', defaultState 'on', risk 'medium', cost 'medium', action 'prepare'. Checklist: 'agree who may create templates'. The standard assigns act-now to launched automatic changes with medium risk or cost and a decision to take.
claims.fix: Change front matter action from 'prepare' to 'act-now': on 24 November 2026 the feature is launched and on by default, and the briefing identifies a template-ownership decision to take.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table represents the checklist's instruction to check Copilot licence assignments.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm which users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence'. The only controls row is 'A switch specific to structured document generation'; no licence-assignment row appears.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Confirm which users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, since form creation requires one per the notice and the Learn page.' Retain the verified licence prerequisite elsewhere; do not add a control row.

claims.claim: The Copilot in SharePoint page says its preview PowerShell availability controls are being retired.
claims.quote: The PowerShell cmdlets used to opt tenants and sites in or out during preview are retiring. Existing settings are honored until November 1, 2026.

claims.claim: The feature supports standardised documents such as contracts, agreements and offer letters.
claims.quote: Legal and compliance - Contracts, NDAs, statements of work, settlement agreements, vendor agreements. ... Human resources - Employment verification letters, offer letters, travel and visa support letters.

claims.claim: The workflow starts with licensed template creators, followed by form submitters generating documents.
claims.quote: The document generation process involves two roles and a handoff between them. Content manager (template creator) - Creates and governs templates and forms. ... Content consumer (form submitter) - Submits forms to generate documents.
